chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Salim ibn al-Baraa, popularly known as Ibn al-Ji'abi, may Allah bless him with mercy, reported to us from Abul Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Saeed al-Hamdani, popularly known as Ibn Uqdah, who reported from Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Shayban, who reported from Muhammad ibn Marwan al-Dhuhali, from Amru ibn Saif al-Azdi, who said: Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both, said to me:
"Do not abandon seeking your sustenance from its lawful sources, for it is a support for you upon your religion. And tie your camel, then place your trust in God."
ai.seo_question: According to Imam al-Sadiq, why should one never abandon seeking lawful sustenance?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (as) advises through a chain of narrators to never abandon seeking lawful sustenance, as it strengthens one's faith. He concludes with the well-known prophetic counsel: "Tie your camel and then place your trust in God" — emphasizing that reliance on God must be paired with practical effort. This teaching was given in the context of early Muslim society where economic self-sufficiency was considered a religious duty.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 1. He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Salim ibn al-Baraa, popularly known as Ibn al-Ji’abi, may Allah bless him with mercy, reported to me from Abul Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Saeed al-Hamdani, popularly known as Ibn Uqdah, who reported from Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Shayban, who reported from Muhammad ibn Marwan al-Dhuhali, from Amru ibn Saif al-Azdi who said: Abu Abdillah Ja’far ibn Muhammad (as told me:
"Do not abandon seeking your subsistence from its legitimate sources, for that helps you remain on your faith. And fasten your camel (first), and then entrust (it to) Allah."
